title: Lesson 1: Getting Started with Linux
content:
Welcome to Linux Classroom!

You're now in a fully functional Linux environment. Let's start with the basics.

Try these commands:

pwd - Show your current directory (Print Working Directory)

ls - List files in the current directory

whoami - Show your username

date - Display current date and time

title: Lesson 2: Exploring Files and Directories
content:
Navigating the File System

Linux organizes files in a tree-like structure. Let's learn to navigate:

ls -la - List all files with details (including hidden files)

cd ~ - Go to your home directory

cd / - Go to the root directory (top level)

cd .. - Go up one directory level

cd - - Go back to previous directory

title: Lesson 3: Creating Files and Directories
content:
Managing Your Workspace

Let's create some files and directories:

mkdir my_project - Create a new directory called 'my_project'

cd my_project - Enter the new directory

touch hello.txt - Create an empty file

echo "Hello Linux!" > hello.txt - Write text to the file

cat hello.txt - Display file contents

title: Lesson 4: Editing Files
content:
Working with Text Editors

Linux has several text editors. Let's try the simplest ones:

Nano (easy):

nano myfile.txt - Open nano editor

In nano: Ctrl+O to save, Ctrl+X to exit

Vim (advanced):

vim myfile.txt - Open vim editor

In vim: Press 'i' to insert, Esc then ':wq' to save and quit

Quick editing:

echo "Line 1" > file.txt - Create/overwrite file

echo "Line 2" >> file.txt - Append to file

title: Lesson 5: File Operations
content:
Copying, Moving, and Deleting

Learn to manage your files:

cp file.txt copy.txt - Copy a file

mv file.txt newname.txt - Rename or move a file

rm file.txt - Delete a file (careful!)

rm -r directory/ - Delete a directory and its contents

ls -lh - List files with human-readable sizes

title: Lesson 6: Getting Help
content:
Linux Help System

Linux has built-in help for commands:

man ls - Show manual page for 'ls' command

ls --help - Quick help for any command

whatis ls - Brief description of a command

Classroom Help Commands:

quick-help - Show classroom quick reference

classroom-info - Show your container information

linux-tutorial - Interactive beginner tutorial

title: Lesson 7: Introduction to Python
content:
Your First Python Program

Python is already installed in your container. Let's try it:

python3 --version - Check Python version

python3 - Start Python interactive mode

In Python interactive mode:

>>> print("Hello from Python!")

>> exit() - Exit Python

Create a Python script:

echo 'print("Hello World!")' > hello.py

python3 hello.py - Run the script

title: Lesson 8: Python Basics
content:
Variables and Operations

Let's learn Python basics:

echo '# Variables in Python' > vars.py

echo 'name = "Student"' >> vars.py

echo 'age = 20' >> vars.py

echo 'print(f"Hello {name}, you are {age} years old")' >> vars.py

python3 vars.py - Run the script

Python lists:

echo 'fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]' >> list_demo.py

echo 'for fruit in fruits:' >> list_demo.py

echo ' print(fruit)' >> list_demo.py

title: Lesson 9: Introduction to Rust
content:
Your First Rust Program

Rust is a systems programming language. It's already installed:

rustc --version - Check Rust compiler version

cargo --version - Check Cargo (Rust package manager)

Create a Rust project:

cargo new hello_rust - Create new project

cd hello_rust - Enter project directory

cargo run - Build and run the project

This will compile and run the "Hello, world!" program.

title: Lesson 10: Rust Basics
content:
Understanding Rust Code

Let's look at the generated Rust code:

cat hello_rust/src/main.rs - View the Rust source code

You'll see:

fn main() {
    println!("Hello, world!");
}

Modify the program:

echo 'fn main() { println!("Hello from Rust in Linux Classroom!"); }' > hello_rust/src/main.rs

cd hello_rust && cargo run - Run the modified program

title: Lesson 11: Working with Permissions
content:
Understanding Linux Permissions

Linux has a permission system for security:

ls -la - Notice the first column shows permissions

Example: -rw-r--r--

- First character: file type (- for file, d for directory)

- Next 3: owner permissions (read, write, execute)

- Next 3: group permissions

- Last 3: others permissions

chmod +x script.sh - Make a file executable

chmod 644 file.txt - Set specific permissions

title: Lesson 12: Finding Files and Text
content:
Search Tools

Learn to find what you need:

find . -name "*.txt" - Find all .txt files in current directory

find /home -type f -name "*.py" - Find Python files in /home

grep "hello" file.txt - Search for "hello" in file.txt

grep -r "function" . - Recursively search for "function" in all files

locate filename - Find files by name (if database is updated)

title: Lesson 13: Process Management
content:
Managing Running Programs

Learn about processes:

ps - Show your processes

ps aux - Show all processes

htop - Interactive process viewer (press q to quit)

kill [PID] - Terminate a process by ID

sleep 60 & - Run a command in background

jobs - List background jobs

fg - Bring background job to foreground

title: Lesson 14: Environment Variables
content:
System Configuration

Environment variables store system settings:

echo $HOME - Show home directory path

echo $PATH - Show command search path

env - Show all environment variables

Set your own variable:

export MY_NAME="Student" - Create a variable

echo $MY_NAME - Use the variable

Make it permanent (for session):

echo 'export MY_COURSE="Linux101"' >> ~/.bashrc

title: Lesson 15: Package Management
content:
Installing Software

Ubuntu uses apt for package management:

sudo apt update - Update package lists (sudo may not work for student)

apt list --installed - List installed packages

Python packages with pip:

pip install cowsay - Install a fun Python package

python3 -c "import cowsay; cowsay.cow('Hello!')" - Use it

Rust packages with cargo:

Add dependencies to Cargo.toml, then cargo build

title: Lesson 16: Networking Basics
content:
Network Commands

Basic network troubleshooting:

ping -c 4 google.com - Test connectivity (Ctrl+C to stop)

ifconfig or ip addr - Show network interfaces

curl https://example.com - Fetch web page content

wget https://example.com/file.txt - Download a file

Classroom networking:

myip - Show your container IP address

ssh student@[classmate_ip] - Connect to classmate's container

title: Lesson 17: Shell Scripting Basics
content:
Automate Tasks with Scripts

Create your first shell script:

echo '#!/bin/bash' > myscript.sh

echo 'echo "Hello from shell script!"' >> myscript.sh

echo 'echo "Today is $(date)"' >> myscript.sh

chmod +x myscript.sh - Make it executable

./myscript.sh - Run the script

Script with arguments:

echo '#!/bin/bash' > greet.sh

echo 'echo "Hello $1!"' >> greet.sh

chmod +x greet.sh

./greet.sh Student - Pass an argument

title: Lesson 18: Version Control with Git
content:
Introduction to Git

Git is installed in your container:

git --version - Check Git version

Basic Git workflow:

mkdir mygitproject && cd mygitproject

git init - Initialize repository

echo "# My Project" > README.md

git add README.md - Stage file

git commit -m "Initial commit" - Commit changes

git status - Check repository status

title: Lesson 19: Text Processing Tools
content:
Powerful Text Manipulation

Linux has powerful text processing tools:

cat file.txt | wc -l - Count lines in file

cat file.txt | head -5 - Show first 5 lines

cat file.txt | tail -5 - Show last 5 lines

sort file.txt - Sort lines alphabetically

uniq file.txt - Remove duplicate lines

cut -d',' -f1 data.csv - Extract first column from CSV

tr 'a-z' 'A-Z' < file.txt - Convert to uppercase

title: Lesson 20: Congratulations!
content:
You've Completed the Basics!

Great job completing these lessons! You now have a solid foundation in Linux, Python, and Rust.

What's next?

1. Practice regularly - use the terminal daily

2. Build small projects - create scripts, programs

3. Explore man pages - man is your friend

4. Join Linux communities - ask questions, learn from others

Remember these classroom commands:

quick-help - Quick reference

linux-tutorial - Interactive tutorial

classroom-info - Container information

Happy learning and coding!
